newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen staying strong this week.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen staying strong this week.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell on Monday but gains by certain heavyweights pushed the main market up 0.1 percent and analysts said the bourse this week would likely extend its current run which has brought it to 15,441 points.

"If today's session was a correction it shows how strong the market is -- there wasn't even a (market) fall and the bourse set another record. Tomorrow could be a kind of correction as today, but on the week the market looks strong, said Artur Czerwonski, of Bank Pekao SA brokerage SA.
Analysts said the market, which has set four straight 33-month highs, could find resistance at 16,000 points.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.1 percent to 15,441.0 points and turnover fell 32.4 percent to 143 million zlotys ($49.2 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 44 to 31 with nine stocks flat.
Analysts said prices were apparently rising on demand from institutional investors acting on their new picks for 1997.
Some analysts said rises might also be due to expected good December company earnings from banks and consumer-goods firms benefitting from Poland's recent high credit demand.
Most company earnings are due early next week.

Analysts said top-gainer Petrobank, up the maximum ten percent in moderate trade, was the latest firm to enjoy an exaggerated surge amid the good market mood. Drugs maker Polfa Kutno, up 9.6 percent, extended last week's surge.
Some said Petrobank may have been helped by newspaper reports that majority owner LG Group could form a joint venture with Poland's largest fuel distributor.

Mass privatisation NFI units rose 2.6 percent to 156 zlotys ($53.7) in 31.7-million-zloty ($10.9 million) trade and fell 0.6 percent to 160 zlotys ($55.1 million) in 27.3-million-zloty ($9.4 million) live trade.
